newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.

text.p: April 17 - U.S. stock index futures ended mostly lower, with June S&P 500 futures driven lower by local selling, traders said. June failed to challenge last week's high at 774.60 on early rally, causing some technical disappointment later, traders said. Traders call volume overall moderate. One floor source calls selloff "not overly busy."

Near midday, June made a run for the two-week high set last week at 774.60, but fell 1.00 point short of there. Many floor traders had said that was a key level to determine the near-term direction of the market.

The lower close for June breaks the trend of three consecutive days of higher closes. After sliding to a 4-1/2-month low on Friday, the market has steadily marched higher, more than erasing Friday's steep losses.
Some said the market was due for profit-taking after three days of gains. Others said the intermediate bear trend was still intact.
One trader said the late afternoon decline was not "overly busy" and called overall volume moderate on the day.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange estimated S&P 500 futures volume at 77,776 contracts on Thursday, versus 86,639 traded on Wednesday.
Earlier in the day, various data buoyed debt futures. The firm June T-bond tone spilled into stock index futures.
Bonds gained ground on a rise in the latest weekly jobless claims to 332,000 in the April 12 week from a revised 324,000 in the prior week.
The Philadelphia Fed's business activity index fell to 5.7 in April from 21.1 in March, new orders dropped to 10.5 from 18.8, and shipments eased to 19.0 from 23.9 in March.

At the close, June S&P 500 futures were down 2.20 points at 766.10, Nasdaq 100s were up 6.00 points to 815.00, Russell 2000s were up 0.25 point at 343.85, KCBT Value Line futures fell 1.50 points to 689.50, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 5.0 to 18,085.0 and Midcap 400s lost 0.50 point to 253.50.
